# GoldenRetriever Examples

> GoldenRetriever is the applied examples and integration surface for Retriever: perception, memory, language, composition, simulator/visualization demos, and Hub-loadable robotics type packs.

Use this page when you want examples after understanding the core Retriever runtime.

## Start Here

- Golden overview: https://retriever-space.pages.dev/
- Example guide overview: https://retriever-space.pages.dev/examples/
- Perception and memory: https://retriever-space.pages.dev/examples/perception_and_memory_v1/
- Language and grounding: https://retriever-space.pages.dev/examples/language_and_grounding_v1/
- Pipeline composition: https://retriever-space.pages.dev/examples/pipeline_composition_v1/
- Simulation and visualization: https://retriever-space.pages.dev/examples/simulation_and_visualization_v1/
- Robotics typing overview: https://retriever-space.pages.dev/robotics_typing_standard/
- Hub sharing profile: https://retriever-space.pages.dev/robotics_typing_standard/03_hub_sharing_profile/
- Core docs: https://openretriever-docs.pages.dev/

## Core Boundary

GoldenRetriever is not the core runtime. The runtime package is `retriever-core` and imports as `retriever`. GoldenRetriever owns applied examples and reusable robot-facing type packs.

## Current Hub Type-Pack Direction

The core runtime provides registry and Hub mechanics. GoldenRetriever provides applied types such as `WorldState`, `BeliefGraph`, `Skill`, `Plan`, `Trajectory`, and Arrow conversion helpers as a Hub-loadable pack.

Expected future reference:

```python
from retriever import hub

WorldState = hub.use("openretriever/golden-retriever:WorldState")
```

If a source link is not yet publicly accessible, use the docs pages first; source visibility is the final public-release toggle.

## Agent Guidance

- Start from `AGENTS.md` in the GoldenRetriever repository.
- Use docs pages for public behavior and examples.
- Do not treat experimental lanes as stable unless their page marks them as promoted.
- Do not include private notes or local filesystem paths in public docs.
